Based on my search, I found the official investment objective for the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (MTUM).

## Official Investment Objective

> "The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (the "Fund") seeks to track the investment results of an index composed of U.S. large- and mid-capitalization stocks exhibiting relatively higher price momentum."

This objective is presented in essentially identical form across multiple official sources:

- **iShares.com (official product page):** "The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF seeks to track the investment results of an index composed of U.S. large- and mid-capitalization stocks exhibiting relatively higher price momentum."
- **The Fund's Summary Prospectus / official documentation** confirming the same language.

### Source Citation

**iShares by BlackRock**, "iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF | MTUM — Investment Objective," iShares.com product page: https://www.ishares.com/ch/professionals/en/products/251614/ishares-msci-usa-momentum-factor-etf

**Additionally**, the wording is corroborated in the official iShares Summary Prospectus document for MTUM, available via: https://www.ishares.com/us/literature/summary-prospectus/sp-ishares-edge-msci-usa-momentum-factor-etf-7-31.pdf (and streamed via the iShares US page: https://www.ishares.com/us/library/stream-document?stream=reg&product=I-MTUM...).

The prospectus also adds the more detailed technical statement: "The Fund seeks to track the investment results of the Underlying Index before fees and expenses of the Fund," referring to the MSCI USA Momentum SR Variant Index.

### Key Supporting Facts
- **Ticker:** MTUM
- **Fund Manager:** iShares by BlackRock (BFA)
- **Benchmark/Underlying Index:** MSCI USA Momentum SR Variant Index
- **Expense Ratio:** 0.15%
- **Focus:** U.S. large- and mid-capitalization stocks exhibiting relatively higher price momentum (a factor/momentum strategy)

The most authoritative and citable source is the **official iShares product page** and the **Fund's Summary Prospectus** filed with the SEC, both of which state the investment objective verbatim as quoted above.
